text:
Alice M.: heads-up: production serving cluster A is spiking 503s across a few pods. stacktraces show CUDA illegal memory access (misaligned address) + container OOMs. observed ~10 nodes in the last 12m. tagging @Oncall Eng :rotating_light:
sre-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-032 - sev2 - "GPU node flapping / cuda illegal memory". Pager duty notified to Oncall Eng. Links: https://internal.incidents/redwood/INC-2026-032
Ben K.: taking - jumping into logs, pulling recent crash dumps. which model is primary on these pods?
Alice M.: mostly embedder-worker and runtime-gpt-small quantized variants. noisy in us-west-2a.
Nina (ML Runtime): I see repeated logs: "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: misaligned device address" coming right before container OOM and then kube OOM kill. stack indicates kernel/device pagewalk faults during KV cache evictions.
Luis (SRE): oncall checklist: cordon affected nodes, drain safe, disable autoscaler for the node pool, set routing fallback. I'm going to cordon three nodes (us-west-2a-xx).
Carmen R.: customer-facing: several high-traffic customers reported 20-40% increased latency and ~3% 5xx rate during the spike. I'm preparing a short note.
Oncall Eng: cordoned nodes us-west-2a-{12,14,18}. starting drains now. Will redeploy pods to other AZs.
Ben K.: collecting coredumps and nvidia-smi logs. dumping kernel trace:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, PID=24231, 0x00000000
[ 1234.568000] cuda: illegal memory access at 0x7f5c2a000000
[ 1234.568111] device 3b:00.0: pagewalk error: misaligned pte
```
Ben K.: note: Xid 79 + misaligned pte pattern. looks like eviction race where page table entries are stale while GPU does pagewalk.
Nina (ML Runtime): reproducer attempt locally with heavy prefix eviction + batch mixing shows intermittent illegal access on quantized kernels. may be exposing kernel driver race under high eviction churn.
Alice M.: immediate mitigations: 1) reduce max_batch_size for affected services to lower memory pressure 2) pin model variant to non-quantized fallback for critical tenants 3) enable KV cache sticky mode to reduce eviction churn. Anyone objections?
Luis (SRE): +1. Doing (1) now. Patch config:
```
# temporary rollout
service.runtime.max_batch_size: 8 -> 4
service.embedder.variant: fallback-v1 (non-quant)
```
Oncall Eng: rolled batch cap to 4 on route /generate and /embed. redirecting 10% traffic to standby region per runbook.
Carmen R.: sending status update to impacted customers: "We are investigating intermittent GPU crashes causing elevated error rates. Mitigation in progress — we'll update in 30min."
Customer Success Bot: sent 3 customer notices (CUST-4021, CUST-5089, CUST-6120).
Ben K.: found kernel oops in dmesg on node us-west-2a-12: "pte misalign at unregister_kmm" — filing with infra-driver team. attaching trace: https://internal.logs/gpu/dmesg/3791234567
Nina (ML Runtime): suggestion: fallback routing policy to smaller model (gpt-small-lite) for non-critical routes to avoid high memory kernels during the hot window. Starting a canary with 5% traffic.
Alice M.: good. also enable software-side guard: abort on illegal access and restart container quickly so orchestrator can move it off-host. That reduces cascading evictions.
Luis (SRE): implemented liveness tweak and reduced restart backoff to 10s for the affected pods. forcing node reboots on the three cordoned nodes after data collection.
Oncall Eng: nodes rebooted and returned to Ready in ~8m. after reboot, no new CUDA illegal logs on those hosts.
Ben K.: still seeing a small tail of errors from older pods that were scheduled on other nodes. continuing to scrub logs.
Nina (ML Runtime): runtime team will push a short-lived kernel-level mitigation: disable asynchronous eviction path in our CVM build (flag: --eviction-sync) to avoid race. building image now.
Alice M.: timeline update: first spikes @3791234567; mitigations (batch cap, fallback model, sticky cache) applied by +18m; node cordon/drain/reboot done by +28m; Xid events drop sharply after reboots.
Carmen R.: customer update draft: "Mitigation reduced errors; full postmortem and timeline will follow. If you saw errors, we will include impact window and credits." queueing for review.
Luis (SRE): driver team acknowledged a plausible kernel race under heavy pagewalk churn. they're triaging with vendor (NV). filed ticket: NV-2026-887.
Oncall Eng: capturing next steps: 1) keep batch cap and sticky cache for 24h, 2) rollout kernel driver upgrade when NV provides patch, 3) test --eviction-sync in staging for 48h, 4) postmortem in 72h.
Ben K.: saving all crash dumps to /artifacts/incidents/3791234567/ and snapshotting kernel logs.
Nina (ML Runtime): quick note: quantized kernels are highly memory/time sensitive — fallback model increased memory headroom and eliminated illegal accesses in canary. we'll add an eval to detect misaligned-kernel-sensitive workloads in Optimize.
Alice M.: thanks team. I'll own postmortem and customer impact. tagging @Luis (SRE) for driver follow-up and @Nina (ML Runtime) for runtime mitigations.
Oncall Eng: handing off to SRE lead for long-term action. I'm clear for now. :white_check_mark:
Customer Success Bot: final customer update sent at +1h: "Errors largely mitigated; ongoing monitoring. We'll provide full root cause and credit details after internal postmortem."
Alice M.: closing incident channel note: monitoring for 3h window; will keep retention open until postmortem complete. file: https://internal.postmortems/incidents/3791234567
